# Workflow corpus coverage (corpus-20261006)

*Generated by `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` from `items.jsonl` (1342 items, sha256 `b968d16807847a0d…`; see MANIFEST.json). Status: development/diagnostic corpus for ROADMAP §4.4, not sealed evaluation evidence. Every graph, feature and IR verdict below is a static-analysis heuristic over normalized graphs. Nothing was compiled into Foundry IR or executed, and no oracle was run.*

Reproduce: `cd research/corpus-20261006 && node scripts/merge-items.mjs && node scripts/check-items.mjs items.jsonl --canonical && node scripts/coverage-report.mjs`.

## 1. Merge

- **Inputs:** `parts/automation.jsonl` 396, `parts/orchestration.jsonl` 400, `parts/science.jsonl` 278, `parts/consumer-creative.jsonl` 273 lines (1347 total).
- **Checker:** `scripts/check-items.mjs` validates every line against ITEM-SCHEMA.md (keys, enums, URL/date/licence fields, dangling or duplicate edges, summary length, credential-shaped strings, non-redistributable text) and, with `--canonical`, the merged conventions below. The only failures in the parts were 86 URLs containing spaces (Langflow starter projects, a few ComfyUI files), fixed by percent-encoding. All repairs: url-percent-encoded 86, copyleft-made-non-redistributable 30, connector-template-fragment-dropped 1 (examples in merge-log.json).
- **Dropped:** 0 invalid lines; 5 duplicates (same platform, identical normalized graph and the same title or description): `dify:mkt-dcb096ae-5bb5-4409-946c-49277d53023f`, `airflow:apache-airflow-providers-teradata/tests/system/teradata/examp…`, `airflow:apache-airflow-providers-common-ai/src/airflow/providers/comm…`, `gitlab-ci:gitlab-org/gitlab/lib/gitlab/ci/templates/Jobs/Deploy.lates…`, `gitlab-ci:gitlab-org/gitlab/lib/gitlab/ci/templates/Security/SAST.git…`. 10 groups of identical graphs with different titles and descriptions were kept (e.g. Argo conditional-artifacts/-parameters).
- **One redistribution policy:** the consumer-creative converters treated GPL-3.0 as redistributable while the orchestration and science converters did not. The merge applies the conservative rule everywhere (copyleft, share-alike and non-commercial licences keep only URL, title, a written description, the derived graph with type-level summaries and features): 30 items changed (ComfyUI and Home Assistant GPL-3.0, one MPL-2.0 GitLab project).
- **Features recomputed** from the graph for every item: nodeCount, edgeCount, maxFanOut (distinct successors), humanSteps, effects, hasCode, hasModelCalls. Source-derived features (branching guards, runtime fan-outs, inlined sub-workflows, connectors, domains) cannot be recovered from the graph and are carried from the converters, floored at the graph counts (branching >= condition nodes, loops >= loop nodes, subworkflows >= sub-workflow nodes); `async` gains `wait` when the graph has wait nodes and the trigger kind of every trigger construct. Changed values: async automation 17, orchestration 42; maxFanOut consumer-creative 27; connectors consumer-creative 1.
- **IR verdicts recomputed** with one vocabulary (section 4). 637 verdict strings changed, most of them only renamed or reformatted; 87 items moved from via-extension to native and none moved the other way: Airflow `schedule=@once` system tests (a one-shot start is a run input), sub-workflows that converters inline at compile time (KFP nested pipelines, ComfyUI subgraphs), fixed-count retries (n8n/Dify/Activepieces fit IR `retry`), runtime list fan-out (IR `map`), and the 500-node limit applied to the normalized graph rather than to the source action count.
- **Graph artefacts:** 26 graphs have cycles over data/control edges that come from static edge inference (Snakemake wildcard matching, ComfyUI subgraph instance wiring, one GitLab stage barrier), not from loops in the source. They are kept as converted and noted in `ir.notes`; they do not count as `unstructured-cycle`.

## 4. IR verdicts and missing constructs

Verdicts are computed against the Phase 1 IR (`schemas/workflow.schema.json`, `research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md`): node kinds task, assert, human, map (parallel, `concurrency` <= 16, `failure` fail_fast|collect, `maxItems` <= 1000), loop (bounded, `until`), wait (`delayMs` <= 1 h), agent (one narrow typed model call), code (sandboxed pure JS/Python), verify; per-node `when`, `retry` (<= 10 attempts, <= 60 s backoff), `onError` stop|continue, `join` all_success|all_resolved; <= 500 nodes per flow. `native` = every construct maps onto these by a local rewrite; `via-extension:<a>+<b>` lists the constructs that need an addition; `unsupported:<reason>` = not expressible even with the ROADMAP §2.1 additions.

Overall: native 476 (35%), via-extension 864 (64%), unsupported 2 (unsupported:interactive-dashboard-state).

Reading the tables:

- **Triggers are the most common need** (521 items, 39%): automation 69%, consumer-creative 37% and CI items start on a schedule, webhook or event. Phase 1 has no start condition; a `triggers` block is already planned in ROADMAP §2.1. Only 201 of the 521 need nothing else; the rest also need another construct.
- **`subworkflow-call` unlocks the most items on its own** (102 items have it as their only blocker: Apple Shortcuts `Run Shortcut`, CWL/Snakemake sub-workflows by reference, n8n Execute Workflow, Home Assistant `script.*`). It is `call` in ROADMAP §2.1; statically resolvable callees can be inlined today, the extension matters for reuse, separate run records and recursion (shortcuts that call themselves).
- **Failure handling** (252 items: `error-branch` 220, `completion-hook` 88, `adaptive-retry` 94) has no ROADMAP item. Partial emulations exist: the runtime completes a failed node with `onError:"continue"` as `{ok:false,error}` (src/runtime.mjs), so node-level routes can be written as `when` guards on that output, and a teardown can use `join:"all_resolved"` if every upstream node continues on error. There is no status-aware guard, no run-level `finally` and no attempt-dependent retry. In nf-core: adaptive-retry 72/72, completion-hook 64/72, error-branch 60/72.
- **Agent-session constructs** (`agent-tool-loop`, `chat-session`, `cross-run-state`; 202 items) come from n8n 78, flowise 35, node-red 24, langflow 23, dify 20. Phase 1 `agent` is deliberately one typed call without tools; tool loops map to the ROADMAP `executor` node, while sessions and cross-run state have no specification yet.
- **Schema bounds hit by real items:** `flow-size>500` (12 items: large shortcuts, ComfyUI and Home Assistant graphs) and `durable-wait` (38 Home Assistant items with delays or wait-for-trigger timeouts over 1 h). Not measurable statically: whether runtime fan-outs exceed `map.maxItems` = 1000 (e.g. scatter over genomic intervals) or need more than 16-way concurrency.

## 5. The 30 most complex items

Score = log2(1+nodes) + log2(1+edges) + 1.5·log2(1+branching) + 1.5·log2(1+loops) + 2·log2(1+human steps) + |async| + log2(1+sub-workflows) + 0.5·distinct categories + 0.5·missing constructs + 1 if model calls + 0.5 if code + log2(1+depth). It rewards variety of constructs over raw size. At most 5 items per platform so the list spans platforms; uncapped, the top 30 are apple-shortcuts 24, gitlab-ci 2, home-assistant 2, nf-core 2.

## 6. Recurring motifs and candidate standard operators

Mining is over node labels: the category, with actions split by effect (`read`, `write`, `ext-call`), code split into pure `code` and effectful `script`, conditions as `branch`; workflow inputs/parameters are left out. Path motifs are label sequences along data/control/loop edges with runs of the same label merged (so a chain of ten writes counts as one `write`), length 2–4; support = number of items containing the motif. Each motif is counted once per item.

Observations:

- **operators.md shapes occur, mostly in the LLM app builders.** model → code: 204 items, main cluster automation 64%; classify → route: 80 items, main cluster automation 68%; map with a model body: 61 items, main cluster automation 90%; generate → verify loop: 51 items, main cluster automation 88%; parallel model calls that re-join: 128 items, main cluster consumer-creative 46%. Evidence → hypothesis → check is rare (16 items) and pairwise judgment cannot be told apart from map-reduce by structure. The set fits model-heavy workflows; it says little about the plumbing that dominates human-built ones.
- **Plumbing shapes that operators.md does not name dominate.** Scatter → gather: 787 items, main cluster science 33%; fan-in to one aggregate: 481 items, main cluster science 40%; fetch → transform → write: 104 items, main cluster consumer-creative 39%; trigger → guard → act: 44 items, main cluster automation 66%; poll-until: 101 items, main cluster automation 48%; approval gate: 81 items, main cluster consumer-creative 79%; menu dispatch: 74 items, main cluster consumer-creative 89%; notify-on-failure: 88 items, main cluster orchestration 68%. Almost all are expressible natively today.
- **Candidate standard operators** are the shapes that carry a check of their own and recur across clusters: poll-until (bounded `loop` over `wait` + task with an `until` and a timeout), approval gate (typed `human` answer, timeout routing), scatter-gather (`map` with `failure:"collect"` and a verify over the aggregate), filter-act (guard in `code`, effect as a task with an idempotency key) and notify-on-failure (needs the failure-handling bundle). Each is admitted only after it passes its own executable check in the library (ROADMAP §2.7), not because it is frequent.
- Retrieve → generate (181 items, main cluster automation 61%) and prompt chains (279 items, main cluster automation 66%) map to agent nodes with untrusted-labelled inputs; they need the context compiler's label rules more than a new operator.

| T0 | 374 | no plausible executable oracle at reasonable cost: ComfyUI (GPU and model weights), IFTTT (closed services), science pipelines without shipped tests (mocked bioinformatics tools would check only the call graph), or > 60 nodes without a shipped check |

The practical route for C0 is to derive fixtures once (recorded connector responses, expected outputs) and then judge the constructed Foundry workflow by running it against mocks (effect-trace and output equivalence), which needs no third-party runtime at grading time.

## 8. Pilot shortlist: construct this workflow from its description, checked by execution

131 items are eligible: redistributable, an original (or dataset-recovered) description of >= 60 characters, 4–60 nodes, an oracle tier of T1–T3, and no missing construct beyond the ones a harness can stand in for (trigger → run input, sub-workflow → inline, error-branch → `onError:"continue"` + `when`, completion-hook → all_resolved join, one-shot signal → `human` node answered by the harness). Ranked by oracle tier (T1 > T2 > T3), construct variety (branching, loops/maps, human, model, code, wait, scatter-gather), description quality and size, then picked with per-cluster quotas (automation 8, orchestration 10, science 6, consumer-creative 6; unused quota goes to the best remaining items), at most 3 per platform, no two items with the same node-type multiset or the same description. Shortlist: 30 items. Development set only: items used to improve builders are not held-out evidence.

The binding constraint is descriptions, not oracles: 63 redistributable T1 items (kubeflow 25, dagster 24, temporal 14) have no usable source description. Writing and freezing a description for each from its README/docstring (provenance `written`, before any construction run) would roughly triple the offline-gradable pool.

Freeze the shortlist, fixtures and pass criteria before any comparative run.

## 9. Limits and unknowns

- All verdicts are structural claims from static conversion; no item was compiled into Foundry IR, so expressibility is plausible, not demonstrated. A per-item IR compilation of the pilot shortlist is the next check.
- Converters differ in granularity (steps vs jobs vs tasks; inlined vs referenced sub-workflows), so cross-platform size comparisons are indicative.
- Licences were read from repository LICENSE files, package metadata, dataset cards or platform terms; per-template authors' terms inside marketplaces were not verified.
- Domain tags are keyword heuristics and over-tag.
- The corpus is development/diagnostic material. Sealed evaluation needs fresh items selected and frozen before any builder is tuned on this set.
